### Graph modes

The graph viewer must support three distinct graph commands. These graphs have
different purposes and must not be treated as alternate labels for the same
visualization.

#### `okf-schema graph`

Generate a graph like `viz.html`, for example the visualization in the Google
Cloud knowledge-catalog `crypto_bitcoin` bundle:

<https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/knowledge-catalog/blob/main/okf/bundles/crypto_bitcoin/viz.html>

This is a general OKF document/relationship graph. It has no imposed
direction or top-to-bottom layer ordering.

#### `okfkb graph`

Interactive visualization and exploration of an OKF knowledge base, showing
the stratified OKFKB layers as represented by `okfkb-mockup-ui.png`.

This graph is directional and laid out from top to bottom:

* Top: Principles
* Downward through the knowledge layers
* Bottom: Findings

The graph highlights:

* Knowledge hierarchy
* Semantic relationships
* Finding lifecycle (Active, Superseded, Contradicted, Archived)
* Traceability from observations to high-level decisions

#### `okfreq graph`

Show the two-layer requirements graph, with the primary focus on navigating
between requirements and their traceability relationships.

This graph is directional and laid out from top to bottom:

* Top: StRS requirements
* Bottom: SwRS requirements

The requirements graph should prioritize requirement navigation over the
broader knowledge-base visualization concerns of `okfkb graph`.

#### Usage

```bash
okfkb graph [OPTIONS]
```

#### Description

`okfkb graph` visualizes an OKF knowledge base as an interactive graph. It consumes a preprocessed JSON model generated by `okfkb preprocess`, eliminating the need to parse Markdown at runtime.

The graph highlights the stratified knowledge hierarchy from Principles down
to Findings, along with:

* Semantic relationships
* Finding lifecycle (Active, Superseded, Contradicted, Archived)
* Traceability from observations to high-level decisions

#### Options

```text
--preprocess            Parse Markdown and generate .okfkb/knowledge.json
--input PATH            Load a preprocessed knowledge JSON
--output DIR            Export a static website
--host HOST             Server host (default: localhost)
--port PORT             Server port (default: 8080)
--open                  Open browser automatically
```

#### Examples

```bash
# Generate the graph model
okfkb graph --preprocess

# Launch the interactive viewer
okfkb graph

# Export a static website
okfkb graph --output site/

# Visualize an existing JSON model
okfkb graph --input build/knowledge.json
```

#### Features

* Interactive Cytoscape visualization
* Hierarchical layouts
* Search and filtering
* Expand/collapse neighborhoods
* Node detail panel
* Status visualization for Findings
* Timeline of superseded and contradicted findings
* Traceability path exploration
* Static HTML export
* Zero-runtime Markdown parsing
